einstellungen.text: You're standing in the middle of the city. And suddenly, every light goes out.
First one street. Then the next one. Then everything.
Ben flicks on his bike light. “Okay. Now it's serious.”
From above, it would look like someone switched off entire countries.
A lot of cell towers have backup batteries. But they often only last a few hours.
Without power, there are no traffic lights. No registers. And eventually, no water pumps.
You keep walking. Mile after mile. It starts to rain.
Somewhere out there is Lina. Alone. In the dark.
“She's smart. Smarter than the two of us put together.”
By the park, it's so dark you can barely see your own hand.
Then you remember something. From back when Lina was little.
You two had a signal. Just you two. Three short whistles.
Whoever hears it whistles back. So you'd never lose each other at the mall.
You stand in the middle of the park. And you whistle. Three short ones.
“Come on. Maybe she's already at your grandpa's.”
You turn around. And then you hear it.
Out of the dark, someone whistles back. Three short ones. Your signal exactly.
